claims.text: The India-New Zealand FTA entered into force on 20 October 2026.
New Zealand removed customs duty across all tariff lines for qualifying Indian exports at entry into force.
At entry into force almost 57 percent of New Zealand exports to India became tariff-free; further tariff reductions are phased in. This is export coverage, not a count of tariff lines.
India excluded sensitive products including dairy from tariff concessions under the agreement.
A tariff is a customs duty on imported goods.
Rules of origin determine whether a good qualifies for preferential tariff treatment; merely shipping it from a partner is insufficient.
Tariff preferences do not remove all other costs or customs, biosecurity and product requirements.

important_distinctions: Zero-duty Indian-export access is a concession by New Zealand; do not label all imports into India duty-free.
Almost 57 percent refers to New Zealand export coverage at launch; do not call it 57 percent of products/tariff lines.
The announcement date, signature date, entry-into-force date and research date differ.
Do not claim automatic retail price reductions, guaranteed jobs/income or unlimited visa access.
Do not insert unrelated election results, geopolitical victory claims or predictions.
